questions.question: Day 8 Practice (Restaurant & Dining Out): When talking about asking for item weight price (on weekends), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'I'?

options.a: I am asking for item weight price right now.
options.b: Apples kg how much cost? yesterday
options.c: How much are these organic apples per kilo?
options.d: Apples kg how much cost?

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option C
Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "How much are these organic apples per kilo?".

questions.question: Day 8 Practice (Restaurant & Dining Out): When talking about making morning tea (by 5:00 PM), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'My sister'?

questions.question: Day 8 Vocabulary (Restaurant & Dining Out): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'run errands'?

options.a: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.b: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.c: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.d: Do short daily trips for chores.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
'run errands' means: do short daily trips for chores. Example: "I need to run errands at the market before dinner."

options.c: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.d: Cancel a planned event or meeting.

questions.explanation:

'call off' means: cancel a planned event or meeting. Example: "They had to call off the afternoon presentation."

questions.question:
Day 8 Translation Scenario 1 (Restaurant & Dining Out):

Telugu: "నా పార్సెల్ ఈ రోజు సాయంత్రానికి డెలివరీ అవుతుందా?"
(Literal attempt: "My parcel today evening delivery becoming?")

options.a: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.b: Will my package be delivered by this evening?
options.c: My parcel today evening delivery becoming?
options.d: I am needing to my parcel today evening delivery becoming?

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural Version: "Will my package be delivered by this evening?"

Use 'Will my package be delivered...' for delivery tracking.

questions.question:
Day 8 Translation Scenario 2 (Restaurant & Dining Out):

Telugu: "ముందుగా సమస్య యొక్క మూలకారణాన్ని కనుగొనాలి."
(Literal attempt: "First problem root cause finding wanted.")

options.a: First problem root cause finding wanted.
options.b: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.c: I am needing to first problem root cause finding wanted.
options.d: First and foremost, we must identify the root cause of the issue.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural Version: "First and foremost, we must identify the root cause of the issue."

Use 'First and foremost' and 'identify the root cause'.

questions.question:
Day 8 Translation Scenario 3 (Restaurant & Dining Out):

Telugu: "నాకు కొంచెం తలనొప్పిగా ఉంది, ఒక గంట సేపు రెస్ట్ తీసుకుంటాను."
(Literal attempt: "To me little headache is there, take rest one hour.")

options.a: To me little headache is there, take rest one hour.
options.b: I have a slight headache; I'm going to rest for an hour.
options.c: I am needing to to me little headache is there, take rest one hour.
options.d: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural Version: "I have a slight headache; I'm going to rest for an hour."

Say 'I have a slight headache' instead of literal translations.

questions.question:
Day 8 Translation Scenario 4 (Restaurant & Dining Out):

Telugu: "ఈ టమాటాలు కేజీ ఎంత? కొంచెం తాజావి ఏరి ఇవ్వండి."
(Literal attempt: "These tomatoes kg how much? Pick give fresh.")

options.a: I am needing to these tomatoes kg how much? pick give fresh.
options.b: These tomatoes kg how much? Pick give fresh.
options.c: How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out fresh ones for me.
options.d: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option C
Natural Version: "How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out fresh ones for me."

Use 'per kilo' for price and 'pick out' for selection.
